title: Residue field extensions of a finite group action are normal, and the decomposition group surjects onto the automorphism group

standard_prerequisites.name: The invariant subring of a finite group action is integrally closed in the ambient ring, so primes lying over a given prime exist and the maximal ideals over a maximal ideal form one orbit
standard_prerequisites.use: Restricts the analysis to the finitely many primes over the chosen prime, which form a single orbit under the group.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a finite product of quotients by the primes in one orbit the Chinese remainder theorem makes the diagonal map surjective
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows an element vanishing at all but one of the primes to be chosen, which is the input to the normality argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: Every finite separable extension admits a primitive element, and any normal extension splits as the tensor product of a purely inseparable and a Galois part
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits the residue field extension into its purely inseparable and Galois parts and produces the element whose degree is compared with the order of the group.

core_obligations: Localize the invariants at the prime below and tensor with the ring to reduce to the case where the prime below is maximal, recording that the decomposition group is the stabilizer of the extended prime and that the residue fields are unchanged (proof lines 32718-32725).

Use the integrality of the ring extension to identify the maximal ideals of the ring with the primes lying over the chosen maximal prime, note from the orbit statement that there are finitely many of them and that they form a single orbit, and use the Chinese remainder theorem to see that the diagonal map to the product of the quotients is surjective (proof lines 32726-32736).

Prove normality of the residue field extension: given an element of the residue field, choose a lift vanishing at all the other primes, form the product of the translates of that lift by the group, observe that its image splits completely into linear factors, and conclude that the minimal polynomial of the original element splits completely as well (proof lines 32738-32751).

Assuming the residue field extension normal, split it into a purely inseparable part and a Galois part, and choose an element of the Galois part generating it when finite or a subfield of degree larger than the order of the group when infinite (proof lines 32753-32762).

Reuse the lift and the polynomial from the normality step to show that every Galois conjugate of the chosen element is the image of a translate of that lift under the decomposition group, which gives surjectivity of the map to the automorphism group in the finite case and the desired contradiction in the infinite case (proof lines 32763-32773).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a maximal prime below by localizing the invariants and tensoring, keeping the decomposition group and the residue fields unchanged (proof lines 32718-32725).
List the finitely many primes over the maximal prime, note that they form one orbit and apply the Chinese remainder theorem to obtain elements vanishing outside one prime (proof lines 32726-32736).

Prove normality of the residue field extension by exhibiting, for each element, a polynomial over the residue field that splits completely and is divisible by the minimal polynomial (proof lines 32738-32751).

Split off the Galois part, choose an element of controlled degree and let the translates of the lift realize every Galois conjugate, giving surjectivity or the contradiction (proof lines 32753-32773).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a finite group acting on a ring and a prime lying over a prime of the invariant subring, and asserts first that the residue field extension is algebraic normal and then that the decomposition group maps onto its automorphism group (statement lines 32703-32716). The proof first reduces to the case where the prime below is maximal, which keeps the decomposition group and the residue fields unchanged, then exploits the single orbit of the primes over it: an element vanishing at all the other primes is chosen through the Chinese remainder theorem, the product of its translates splits completely and forces the required minimal polynomial to split, and the same element is reused after splitting the extension into a purely inseparable and a Galois part to realize every Galois conjugate by a translate under the decomposition group, the infinite case being excluded by a degree count (proof lines 32718-32773). The union of the normality argument and the conjugate realization is what makes the surjectivity statement work.
